title: Home Mortgage Loans: Posting and Application of Borrower Payments
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: Posting and Application of Borrower Payments

When a borrower remits money toward one of the Home Mortgage Loans, the servicing rules decide whether it posts at all and, if it does, how it is split among interest, principal, escrow and fees due. Fees due, on this product, means the late charges and servicing fees the borrower has not yet paid.

## Clauses

**Loans that accept payments.** A payment posts only to a loan that the bank's records show as active, delinquent or in forbearance. A loan standing as applied, paid off or withdrawn takes no payment.

**Remittances below one full installment.** A payment that is less than one full installment is dealt with under the program's setting for such payments, which on every program is to return it: the money goes back to the borrower and nothing of it is applied to the loan.

**Split of each whole installment.** Every full installment contained in a payment is allocated in this order: interest, then principal, then escrow.

**Money beyond whole installments.** Whatever remains after the whole installments goes to fees due, and then, if the remainder reaching that point is at least the program's smallest extra principal payment, to principal as a curtailment.

**Late charges stay outside the installment.** A late charge is never taken out of an installment. A full installment received on time is therefore never turned into a late one because a late charge is still unpaid.

**Payments from a checking account.** When a payment comes from a checking account at Piedmont Crescent Bank, that checking account is debited for the payment.

## Input, judgement, output

| What arrives | Judgement | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Any payment, loan applied, paid off or withdrawn | loan does not take payments | not posted |
| Less than one full installment, loan active, delinquent or in forbearance | below a full installment | returned to the borrower, nothing applied |
| Exactly one full installment | one whole installment | interest, principal, escrow in that order |
| One full installment and an additional amount | whole installment plus excess | installment split as above; excess to fees due, and any part left that meets the program minimum to principal as a curtailment |

## Allocation example (hypothetical amounts)

An imagined loan has a full installment of $1842.25, made up of $1000.00 interest, $432.25 principal and $410.00 escrow, and it carries $60.00 of fees due. The borrower remits $2000.00.

- The whole installment absorbs $1842.25: $1000.00 to interest, $432.25 to principal, $410.00 to escrow.
- The excess is $157.75. Of that, $60.00 clears the fees due.
- The last $97.75 is applied to principal as a curtailment, provided it is not below the program's smallest extra principal payment.

Had the same borrower sent $1800.00, the remittance would be below one full installment and would be returned unapplied.

These amounts are invented for illustration.
